analysis: Docs-only change in docs/architecture/inference.md (head 2336-2348): describes Flint constrained chaining (step N+1 sampled with mask through N-1, redrawn on state change with penalty/RNG restored), maskCacheKey caching device masks by constraint state while output budget remains, and RecursiveSI/flint-int4 on the automatic paged list at legacy serving width on M5 Pro/Max/Ultra. Base units 6-8 (lines 1636-2412) were examined as surrounding context. No threat-model asset (A-001 plaintext, keys, attestation, cache at-rest T-041) or trust boundary is altered by this text; the claims concern output equivalence and performance/concurrency, relevant only tangentially to T-007 (output correctness) and TB-007 availability. Mask caching keyed solely on state is a correctness claim: if the allowed set also depended on remaining budget or per-request stop sequences (FlintAnswerStops, client stop up to 4x256 bytes, line ~2259), a state-only key could misapply masks across requests; doc says key applies 'while output budget remains', and stop state is presumably part of constraint state. This is a source-implementation question (FlintNativeProtocolConstraint.swift, FlintAnswerStopConstraint.swift, CBv2 engine chaining) not supplied here; no evidence of a regression, and impact would be per-request output integrity within one provider, not cross-tenant disclosure, unless mask cache is shared across rows with different stop/tool specs. Integration may verify mask-cache scoping per request/row if source is available. Automatic paged default for Flint changes concurrency but memory admission/context checks remain described (lines 2342-2346).
